clue.text: Graduate taken in by cheeky new first-year student

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so one piece sits within the rest

blocks.note: fresh can mean impudent or forward
a Master of Arts is a graduate
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A cheeky newcomer at university has been taken under the wing of a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graduate taken in by' suggests mentoring; it means the degree sits inside the other two pieces. MA is a Master of Arts degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshman is the usual term for a student in the first year at college or university.

clue.text: I get riled, breaking slab

indicators.note: breaking smashes something apart, so these letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: the letters of these words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits to losing their temper and smashing a paving slab.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge tile is a curved slab of fired clay or concrete laid along the top of a roof.

clue.text: Outcry as Indian language is introduced into school

indicators.note: introduced into means brought inside, so this piece sits within the next one

blocks.note: SCH is a standard abbreviation for school
Cree is spoken by a First Nations people of Canada

explanation.surface: Protest erupts when a Native American tongue is added to a school's curriculum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' here means Native American, not from India: Cree is a North American language.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a loud, shrill cry, as is an outcry in its literal sense.

clue.text: Kid supplied coffee or port

blocks.note: first meaning: a soft leather made from goatskin, kid
second meaning: a fine coffee, originally shipped from Arabia
third meaning: the Red Sea port in Yemen that gave the coffee its name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child; it is the leather. There are three meanings here: the leather, the coffee and the port.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine goatskin leather, a coffee, and the Yemeni harbour town the coffee was exported from.

clue.text: Sister giving grandma a change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart means the middle letter of the word is swapped for another

blocks.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A sister passes something to her grandmother, who changes her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the middle A of NAN for a U.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is a member of a religious order, addressed as Sister.

clue.text: Get into bother, taking a sherry glass

indicators.note: taking means one piece picks up another and carries it along at its end

blocks.note: to cop it is slang for getting into trouble or being punished
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lands in trouble after helping themselves to a sherry glass.
explanation.walkthrough: To cop it is British slang for being punished or getting into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A copita is the tulip-shaped glass traditionally used for drinking sherry in Spain.

clue.text: Taken in by crop circle, he finally is going round the bend

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so this letter sits within the pair that follows
finally points to the last letter of the word, the only one kept

blocks.note: corn is a cereal crop
the last letter of he
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: Someone baffled by crop circles is losing his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round the bend' suggests madness, prompted by the crop circle; it means taking a corner literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornering means taking a corner, that is, driving round a bend.

clue.text: Artist's picture reduced in size: head of poet missing

indicators.note: reduced in size means the word is cut down to a shorter form
the head of a word is its opening letter, which is what goes here
missing means that part is absent, so it is removed from the word

blocks.note: taken as written, then shortened
Torquato Tasso was an Italian Renaissance poet

explanation.surface: A painter's work is shrunk down, with a poet's head cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: Pic is the familiar short form of picture; Tasso wrote the epic Jerusalem Delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso, the Spanish painter and co-founder of Cubism, is among the most famous of artists.

clue.text: Empty trawler available for fish

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of trawler
out can mean on offer, as a book that is out

explanation.surface: A trawler has nothing aboard, so is free to go after fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The trout is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: A mostly unenlightened period for Jewish people

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
in the dark means unenlightened

explanation.surface: A historical claim that some era was a gloomy time for the Jewish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unenlightened period' reads like the Dark Ages, but only 'unenlightened' is wordplay; 'period for Jewish people' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar is a month of the Hebrew calendar, so it is a period of time in the Jewish year.

clue.text: Businessman's scam with vehicle

indicators.note: with means the second piece comes alongside the first, placed right after it

blocks.note: a con is a swindle
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: A businessman is running some fraud involving a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay rather than marking possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A contractor is a person or firm in business supplying work or goods under contract.

clue.text: African seen buffeted by strong winds to the east

indicators.note: something buffeted is knocked about, so its letters are thrown into a new order
in an across entry the east side is the right, so this piece is added at the end

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
gales are strong winds
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An African traveller is spotted being battered by storm winds blowing from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffeted by strong winds' reads as one image, but 'buffeted' acts only on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegalese describes a person from Senegal, a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Female English poet pens drama

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, so the poet holds the next piece inside

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse
No, or Noh, is classical Japanese drama

explanation.surface: A woman poet from England writes a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female English poet' reads as one person; 'Female' is the definition and the poet is a man, Edward Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a woman's first name, so it can stand for a female.

clue.text: Boy's name recurs in French test

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning them
to recur is read as re-cur, running back over the letters from the end

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A boy's name keeps cropping up in a French examination.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'French test' backwards and SETH appears across the join of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth is a male first name, borne in the Bible by the third son of Adam.

clue.text: As tourist, visit place near the ocean, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, so their sound counts, not their spelling

blocks.note: a site is a place
the sea is the ocean

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers go and look at a spot beside the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Site near sea, spoken out loud, matches the verb for touring the sights.
explanation.definitionFit: To sightsee is to visit places of interest as a tourist does.

clue.text: Mixture of drinks that could prove lethal?

blocks.note: first meaning: a pub drink of lager mixed with cider
second meaning: a wound from a venomous serpent's fangs

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a deadly cocktail; the question mark admits the second meaning is a wound, not a drink. In Britain the drink is a half-and-half of lager and cider.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a strong lager-and-cider mix and a venomous bite, which can kill.

clue.text: Duke ensnared by one lone princess

indicators.note: something ensnared is trapped inside, so this piece goes within the word that follows

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
sole means single or alone
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A duke is captured by a solitary princess.
explanation.walkthrough: I, then SOLE with the duke's D trapped near its end: I + SOL(D)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the Irish princess of the Tristan legend, the heroine of Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Doctor I've introduced to fellow is different from the others?

indicators.note: introduced to means brought inside, so this piece goes within the one named before

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
taken as written
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A doctor introduced to a man wonders whether he is unlike the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introduced to' suggests people meeting; here it signals one piece placed inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Divergent means departing from what is usual, so differing from the others.

clue.text: Holy city's name revealed in the papers for instance

indicators.note: something revealed in a thing is shown sitting within it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: newspapers are one example of the media
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A holy city's identity is disclosed in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For instance' marks the papers as one example of a wider class, the media.
explanation.definitionFit: Medina in Saudi Arabia is Islam's second holiest city, burial place of the Prophet.

clue.text: Wow! One million newspapers

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for million
the press means newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: An exclamation of astonishment at a million newspapers sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wow' looks like an exclamation; here it is a verb, to wow someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To wow an audience is to impress it greatly.

clue.text: Snap out of it? Yes-... and no

blocks.note: first meaning: the film image from which a photograph, or snap, is printed
second meaning: a refusal or denial

explanation.surface: Someone is told to snap out of a mood and answers with a hesitant yes and no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap out of it' looks like a command to cheer up; here a snap is a photo, which comes out of a film negative. 'Yes-... and' just answers the question mark before giving the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: In photography a negative is the reversed image prints are made from; in speech a negative is a reply meaning no.

clue.text: Sounds car horn and starts to irritate extremely pretty girl

indicators.note: starts point to the opening letter of each of the next two words

blocks.note: to toot is to sound a horn
the first letters of irritate and extremely

explanation.surface: A driver honks at an attractive woman and annoys her greatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely pretty' looks like a phrase, but extremely belongs with irritate as the source of a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsie is dated slang for an attractive young woman or girlfriend.

clue.text: Keep complaining about queen having power

indicators.note: having means the piece before holds on to the next one, which follows it

blocks.note: ca, short for circa, means about
R, for regina, stands for queen
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles endlessly about a queen holding power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it means 'concerning'; here it is circa, abbreviated CA.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault continually, making petty complaints.

clue.text: Molly heading off unaccompanied

indicators.note: with its heading off, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: Molly Malone is the fishmonger of the Dublin song Cockles and Mussels

explanation.surface: Molly sets off on her way without company.
explanation.walkthrough: The song's heroine Molly Malone wheels her barrow through Dublin; dropping her surname's first letter leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alone means without anyone else present, that is, unaccompanied.

clue.text: Car's route diverted round front of London tube station

indicators.note: a diverted route goes a different way, so these letters take a new order
round means placed around, enclosing the next piece
front of a word is its opening letter, and only that is kept

blocks.note: the letters of these words, to be rearranged
the first letter of London

explanation.surface: A driver's journey is rerouted around the outside of a London Underground station.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters of 'Car's route' wrap round the first letter of London. The tube is London's Underground railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl's Court is a station on the District and Piccadilly lines of the London Underground, known as the tube.

clue.text: Awfully terse piece of advice

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so these letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some guidance was given in a very curt manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A steer is informal for a hint or guidance that points someone in the right direction.

clue.text: Entertainer put directions in invitation to meal

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so these letters go within the phrase that follows

blocks.note: come dine is an invitation to eat
east and north are compass directions

explanation.surface: A performer has written stage directions into a dinner invitation.
explanation.walkthrough: The two compass letters EN slip in between the I and N of COME DINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedienne is a female comedian, so a performer whose job is to entertain.

clue.text: Climbing high mountain, you'll need a breather?

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means the word is read from the bottom up

blocks.note: ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A mountaineer on a high peak will need to stop for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' suggests a rest; with the question mark it is something you breathe through. Neb is a Scots word for nose or beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A neb is a nose, and the nose is the organ one breathes through.

clue.text: Setback suffered by supreme ruler in scene of crisis

indicators.note: a setback sends something backwards, so the next word is turned end to end

blocks.note: Zeus ruled over the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A supreme leader suffers a reverse during a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1956 Suez Crisis saw Britain and France humiliated over the Egyptian canal.
explanation.definitionFit: Suez, the canal zone in Egypt, gave its name to the 1956 crisis, a famous political emergency.

clue.text: Leather strap that is fixed on big girl's blouse.

indicators.note: fixed on means attached to the end, so this piece follows the one before

blocks.note: a jess is a short leather strap fastened to a hawk's leg in falconry
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A leather strap has been attached to a large woman's blouse.
explanation.walkthrough: A big girl's blouse is British slang for a feeble or unmanly man, as is jessie, chiefly Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive British slang for a man thought weak or effeminate, so one can stand in for the other.

clue.text: Front of barge: unusual retreat for lock keeper

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, the only one kept here
unusual means out of the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of barge
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A canal scene: a barge and a strange hideaway for the person who works the lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock keeper' suggests a canal official, which the barge reinforces; the lock is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrette is a hair clip, so it holds a lock of hair in place.
